prompt: Which of these formulas is a tautology (true in every row of its truth table)?
hint: A tautology can never be false. Try P true, then P false.
explanation: P ∨ ¬P is true whether P is true or false, so it is a tautology. P ∧ ¬P is never true, and P → ¬P and P ↔ ¬P are false in at least one row.
